newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up on technical adjustments.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up on technical adjustments.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were quoted higher at the close due to technical adjustments, but demand remained weak with players staying away for festive holidays, traders said.
The extension of the Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr celebrations from last week has left a lull in the market, and the situation was unlikely to change until next week, they said.
"It's virtually dead. The higher prices are just an adjustment to match movements on other markets during the holidays here," said a trader.
At the close, March RSS1 buyer was quoted at 305.50 cents ($) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, up 3.50 cents from February 5. March SMR 20 rose 2.50 cents.
Traders offered the SMR 20 at 295/296 cents a kg, SMR CV at 358, SMR L at 341, SMR 10 at 298 and drum latex FOB at 236/238.
The INRO five-day moving average was at 232.43 Malaysia/Singapore cents ($0.93) a kg on February 5 from 231.88 cents on February 4. The daily indicator was at 233.43 from 232.92 previously.
